Re-check result: Exp15 4.2 is genuinely present. Exp15 4.3 and 4.4 do not hold as stated, and the missed load-balancing findings are:

FINDING_ID: LB_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.94  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: In [bench/dynamic_management.py:805](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L805), `_admissibility_mask()` derives pool cardinality from `role_map` instead of the live `self.models`, and at [bench/dynamic_management.py:818](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L818) it silently defaults missing role entries to `PAR`. Combined with [bench/dynamic_management.py:4927](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4927), this breaks active-pool degradation: a PM-only surviving pool is treated as `K>1`, so the only live PM becomes inadmissible; conversely, an incomplete role map makes unassigned models silently admissible. I verified both cases: one yielded `[[0]]` plus an `F3` violation against the sole PM, and the other yielded `[[1, 1]]` admissibility with a missing role entry.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `set(role_map.keys()) == {m.model_id for m in models}` on `LoadBalancer` construction, compute `K` from `len(self.models)` or the active pool, remove the `PAR` default for unknown models, and have `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` pass a role map filtered to active models.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: The Exp15 “feasibility warning” fix is not actually surfaced to callers. `_solve_greedy()` only appends degraded redundancy notices to private state at [bench/dynamic_management.py:973](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L973), while `solve()` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:1006](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1006) exposes neither those warnings nor any redundancy-feasibility flag. I verified this with `PM + 2 workers` and one critical task: allocation returned `[[0,1,1]]`, `_allocation_warnings` contained `target=3, feasible=2/2`, `_check_feasibility()` returned `(True, [])`, and no external warning was emitted. That means Exp15 4.3/4.4 is still wrong in practice: impossible redundancy silently degrades.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either make unmet redundancy an explicit feasibility check/result field, or redefine `_redundancy_target()` against admissible active executors instead of theoretical pool size. Do not hide the condition in `_allocation_warnings`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: The task-decomposition feedback loop is not actually closed in this repo. `DetectorHealthMonitor.check_dispatch_health()` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:4058](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4058) can only learn from block-then-success histories, but repo-wide search found no call site for `record_dispatch_success_after_block()` beyond its definition at [bench/dynamic_management.py:6053](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L6053). Likewise, `pre_decompose_models` is declared and written, but there is no consumer in planning/dispatch code. Unless external code manually wires both pieces, false-positive blocking never changes future dispatch decisions.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Record successful post-decomposition dispatches automatically, and consume `config.pre_decompose_models` in the planner/dispatcher before raw feasibility gating so learned decomposition state actually affects later routing.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `check_dispatch_feasibility()` still uses `self.fsm.current_round` for event timestamps at [bench/dynamic_management.py:4955](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4955), even though `process_round()` had to introduce its own monotonic counter because `fsm.current_round` lags the actual processed round. I verified the mismatch: after processing round 0, the next blocked-dispatch event was still tagged `round_idx=0` instead of `1`. That corrupts block/success chronology and weakens dispatch-health learning.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass an explicit dispatch round index from the caller, or derive it from the same monotonic counter used in `process_round()`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.75  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: Area-2 threshold ordering is not validated. `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__()` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:199](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L199) never enforces `tau_moderate <= tau_critical`, but `_redundancy_target()` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:827](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L827) assumes that ordering. I verified `DynamicManagementConfig(tau_critical=0.3, tau_moderate=0.8)` is accepted, and then a `criticality=0.5` task is treated as fully critical. This silently rewires the redundancy policy and can make the moderate band unreachable.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `0.0 <= tau_moderate <= tau_critical <= 1.0` in `__post_init__()` and add a regression test for reversed thresholds.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.42  
DESCRIPTION: Core load-balancing dataclasses accept impossible values with no validation. [bench/dynamic_management.py:271](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L271), [bench/dynamic_management.py:309](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L309), and [bench/dynamic_management.py:332](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L332) define `CapabilityFingerprint`, `ModelSpec`, and `Task` with no `__post_init__` guards. I verified that `Task(token_demand=-500)` produces negative load and negative allocation cost, and an out-of-range fingerprint like `(-1, 2, 2, 2)` produces capability scores above `1.0`. That lets impossible loads and rankings enter the allocator unchecked.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add dataclass validation for finite values, nonnegative `tau/L/c/L_std/token_demand`, and bounded `[0,1]` fields such as `criticality`, `D_decay`, `v_bar`, `A`, and `C`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
